gen-eater-gf-recursive: Aggressive and dark up top, Eater pairs thin strokes with moderately weighty stems, spaced wide apart. Recursive below draws a plain sans line like a ballpoint pen would.
gen-eater-gf-roboto-condensed: Contemporary Roboto Condensed packs its sans-serif lowercase tight, the words gliding along like wire under the eye. Eater's gaps and tempered contrast do their best work big and short.
gen-eater-gf-saira-semi-condensed: Dark and jagged, then smooth. Eater carries a middling thick-thin difference, and Saira Semi Condensed brings a plain sans whose text looks magnified. And its unvarying weight is what holds the pair together.
gen-eater-gf-secular-one: Heavy midsections, zero modulation, no fuss. Eater's restrained thick-thin rhythm sits above Secular One's sans-serif line, so a big heading with noticeably smaller text below would let each font do its job.
gen-eater-gf-smooch-sans: Smooch Sans packs its sans line tight, with a high midline and an s that opens generously at each bend. Eater's lightly shaded texture against that low-contrast body is the strongest thing here.
gen-eater-gf-sofia-sans-condensed: Sofia Sans Condensed has a big x-height and strokes like thread stitched along a path, with curves left open where the pen lifted. And Eater's wide gaps and mild modulation above leave the text running smoothly down a page.
gen-eater-gf-spline-sans-mono: Spline Sans Mono reads technical and fixed-width, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals in bold, constant outlines. Spline Sans Mono is the steady monospace partner to Eater's brush stroke, which shows only slight pressure variation.
gen-eater-gf-strait: Strait offers a sans with big round lowercase bowls and low contrast, approachable and contemporary. And Eater's visible but mild contrast above means long text would feel friendly rather than menacing.
gen-eater-gf-tiny5: Tiny5 is a clean, approachable sans-serif whose ascenders look short because the body is so tall. And Eater's slowly thinning arch shoulders make the dark-versus-friendly difference the pair's strongest quality.
gen-eater-gf-truculenta: Eater snarls with a sensible thick-thin difference and wide gaps, while Truculenta crowds rope-fine sans-serif letters into a compact line. And that line stays open to the side, so a long passage would move along comfortably.
